html:
The Mescalero are an Apache people of south-central New Mexico, speaking a Southern Athabaskan language. They lived in the mountains east of the Rio Grande, around Sierra Blanca and the Sacramento Mountains, and hunted on the plains to the east. Their name comes from mescal, the agave they roasted in pits for food.

They raided Spanish and Mexican settlements and fought the United States after it took New Mexico in 1848. In 1863 the US Army forced them onto the Bosque Redondo reservation with the Navajo; most escaped in 1865. In 1873 they got their own reservation in their home mountains.

Other Apache groups later joined them: some Lipan in the early 1900s and, in 1913, many Chiricahua freed after 27 years as prisoners of war. Today they form the Mescalero Apache Tribe. See also Apache.
